questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: “There is hardly any water left, ____?”
questions.why: 'Hardly' makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The population of Goa is smaller than ____ of Maharashtra.”
questions.why: 'That' replaces the singular noun 'population' to avoid repetition. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “recalcitrant”:
questions.why: 'Recalcitrant' means stubbornly resisting authority; obstinate. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said, “If I had known, I would have come.”
opts: He said that if he had known, he would have come.
He said that if he has known, he would come.
He said that if he had had known, he would have come.
He said that if he knew, he would have come.
questions.why: A third conditional is already in the past perfect and does not change. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The committee needs a ____ arbiter who has no stake in the outcome.”
questions.why: 'Disinterested' means impartial; 'uninterested' means bored. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct version: “Let you and I settle this matter at once.”
opts: Let you and me to settle this matter at once.
Let you and I to settle this matter at once.
Let you and me settled this matter at once.
Let you and me settle this matter at once.
questions.why: 'Let' takes the objective case and a bare infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “More than one candidate ____ failed the test.”
questions.why: 'More than one' takes a singular noun and verb. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “You ____ have bought the medicine; we already had it.”
questions.why: 'Needn't have' + past participle means an action done but unnecessary. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “a swan song”:
opts: a final performance or achievement before retirement
questions.why: A swan song is a last appearance or work. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “I saw him enter the room.”
opts: He was seen enter the room by me.
He was seen to entered the room by me.
He saw to enter the room by me.
He was seen to enter the room by me.
questions.why: A bare infinitive after a perception verb becomes a to-infinitive in the passive. GPSC-style practice item.
